figures.name: Puer
figures.imagery: A sword; a male figure with exaggerated testicles
figures.body_type: A compact and athletic frame, with quick gestures and a complexion easily flushed by exertion or weather. The jaw and brow tend to be pronounced, the hairline somewhat uneven, and the hands often bear the small marks of tools, instruments, or contact sport.
figures.traditional_body_type: Historically associated with a compact, sturdy build, prominent musculature, and a ruddy or flushed complexion. Classical texts often note distinct or uneven facial features and a lack of dense facial hair.
figures.character_type: One who acts first and reflects afterward: competitive, blunt of speech, loyal in bursts, and restlessly curious. Such a person resists being managed and tends to find composure only after motion or contest has spent the initial charge.
figures.traditional_character_type: Traditionally described as impulsive, energetic, and prone to acting before thinking. Classical interpretations highlight a hot-tempered, youthful nature that lacks tact or foresight but possesses undeniable courage.
figures.commentary: Puer names the martial impulse that arrives ahead of reflection. The classical authors place the figure under Mars and Aries: outer fire, inner air, with the intellect overrunning its own consequences. Three lines stand active while water rests, so the figure carries heat and edge without the tempering grace of feeling. Its image is not the lover but the engineer of pressure—force in search of a channel. Where the medieval tradition described the young soldier or the duelist, the contemporary practitioner should attend to vectors: who initiates, who escalates, and where the first blow lands. Puer favors questions that turn on decisive intervention and disfavors those that require patience, secrecy, or careful diplomacy.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Swift motion, the opening of a contest, surgical intervention, mechanical repair, or any matter in which force applied early shapes the field.
figures.tagline: Heat at the threshold—courage, hurry, and a blade that wants a sheath

figures.name: Amissio
figures.other_names: Grasping externally, outer wealth, something escaped or lost
figures.imagery: A bag held mouth downward, letting the contents fall out
figures.body_type: A solid neck and a jaw that is either square or softly rounded, with a voice that carries. The shoulders are broader than the hips, and the hands handle weight with practiced ease.
figures.traditional_body_type: Classical sources describe a robust, large-boned frame of average height, often featuring a broad neck, rounded facial structure, and thick, abundant hair. A visible scar or mark is sometimes noted.
figures.character_type: Warm, candid, and given to attachment that runs deeper than pride will easily admit. Such a person dislikes being overlooked and oscillates between open generosity and blunt requests.
figures.traditional_character_type: Historically viewed as emotionally reactive and forthright. Older texts suggest a character driven by immediate attachments and a strong, sometimes inflexible, sense of personal honor, occasionally lacking strict honesty.
figures.commentary: Amissio pictures the purse inverted: a Venusian appetite meeting an earth that cannot keep every coin. Fire and water flare without a steady mediating air, and earth at the rim lies passive, so what is gained slips because the vessel itself is open. The figure speaks not only of poverty but of release—what leaves makes room.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Outflow, ransom, donation, separation, depreciation, the shedding of debt, or the loss of track of an asset.
figures.tagline: What leaves makes room—open purse, shifting worth

figures.name: Albus
figures.body_type: An upper torso held with quiet lift, breathing that remains steady under stress, and a preference for layered clothing. The fingers rest lightly at the keys or stain with ink.
figures.traditional_body_type: Traditionally depicted with a broader upper body narrowing at the waist, a prominent head, and rounded features. Historical texts often attribute a neat or distinguished appearance to this figure.
figures.character_type: One who speaks little but precisely, keeps notebooks, and avoids crowds while building a small network with deliberation.
figures.traditional_character_type: Classically interpreted as gentle, peaceable, and somewhat reserved. Older sources describe a kind-hearted individual who values quiet companionship but may struggle with financial prudence.
figures.commentary: Albus is the bright cup raised without spill: Mercury in Gemini, outer air over inner water, an intellect that mirrors a quiet depth. While the Renaissance standard (Agrippa) assigns this firmly to Mercury and Gemini, older Arabic traditions flowing through Gerard of Cremona sometimes lean toward Lunar or Cancerian rulership due to the 'white', reflective, and peaceful nature of the figure. In practice, Albus marks clarity won by stepping sideways from the fight.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Peaceful progress, study, paperwork that clears, the truce, the diagnosis that finally clarifies, and the gentle rain that follows drought.

figures.name: Populus
figures.body_type: A torso that holds tension at the diaphragm and a gait that subtly synchronizes with whoever walks alongside.
figures.traditional_body_type: Historical descriptions point to a taller, somewhat slender physique with narrower hips and elongated facial features. Classical texts frequently mention distinct marks or slight asymmetries in appearance.
figures.character_type: One who mirrors the company present and whose moods are easily caught by others.
figures.traditional_character_type: Traditionally characterized by a highly receptive and impressionable nature, easily swayed by the crowd. Older interpretations note a strong emotional current and a restless desire for travel or movement.
figures.colors: Sea green or dark russet brown
figures.commentary: Populus is the throng: every line passive, water doubled within and without. The Moon's sign of Cancer underscores collective memory, tide, and the kitchen in which everyone speaks at once. Elementally, nothing initiates; inertia itself becomes stability.
figures.divinatory_meaning: The assembly, the audience, the poll, the household vote, the public mood, or any outcome decided by collective sentiment rather than by a single hand.
figures.tagline: Many voices, one tide—motion borrowed from the whole

figures.name: Fortuna Major
figures.other_names: Inward fortune, protection going in, greater omen, inside or hidden help
figures.imagery: A valley through which a river flows
figures.body_type: Open, deep chest-breathing and warm, steady hands. The posture often shows a small compensation—one leg carried slightly differently from the other.
figures.traditional_body_type: Classically associated with a well-proportioned upper body but occasionally uneven or asymmetrical lower limbs. Historical sources often note a radiant, rounded face with prominent, expressive eyes.
figures.character_type: Generous, quietly proud, and reliable in the keeping of promises. Such a person spends to lift others, dislikes pettiness, and bears responsibility without making a display of it.
figures.traditional_character_type: Historically described as possessing a natural dignity, inherent fairness, and a generous spirit. Older texts highlight an ambitious but honorable nature that enjoys the comforts of wealth.
figures.commentary: Fortuna Major is the sheltered valley that gathers water: Sun in Leo, yet the outer fire rests while inner earth and the active water and earth lines shape the terrain. The help arriving for the querent comes from foundations, elders, savings, or an institution with room enough to absorb shock.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Substantial fortune obtained through persistence, the inheritance of one's own past effort, institutional backing, or an integrity recognized late.
figures.tagline: Deep fortune, sheltered gain, earned stature

figures.name: Conjunctio
figures.body_type: A lithe waist and expressive hands that punctuate speech, with a digestion sensitive to stress.
figures.traditional_body_type: Traditionally depicted as having a delicate, slender, and attractive build. Classical descriptions often emphasize fine facial features, an elegant nose, and an overall nimble appearance.
figures.character_type: One who joins points quickly, takes pleasure in introductions, and is willing to entertain flexibility of means when better information becomes available.
figures.traditional_character_type: Classically viewed as highly communicative, sharp-witted, and socially adept. Historical interpretations often warn of a tendency to prioritize cleverness and networking over strict ethical boundaries.
figures.colors: Purple or pale gray, sometimes black speckled with blue
figures.commentary: Conjunctio is the crossroads at which streams meet: Mercury in Virgo, inner air over outer earth, with air and water carrying the motion. The contemporary practitioner may translate that intuition into the language of supply chains, networks, and the introductions that re-route a vocation. The figure is, by nature, morally mixed.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Networks, mediation, logistics, reconciliations of accounts, the recovery of items through a chain of acquaintances, and conversations that bring previously separate parties into agreement.

figures.name: Puella
figures.imagery: A mirror; a female figure with exaggerated breasts
figures.body_type: A gracefully curved lumbar line, a long neck, and a voice naturally tuned to harmony. The lower back tends to register imbalance before the mind acknowledges it.
figures.traditional_body_type: Historical texts describe a highly symmetrical, graceful, and aesthetically pleasing form. Classical features include large eyes, a clear complexion, and a melodious voice.
figures.character_type: One who seeks equilibrium and possesses a sharp aesthetic judgment. Such a person tends to avoid open conflict until cornered.
figures.traditional_character_type: Traditionally characterized by an intense desire for harmony and a strong aversion to conflict. Older sources paint a portrait of a romantic, artistic soul who may sometimes appear fickle or easily distracted.
figures.commentary: Puella stands in counterpoise to Puer: Venus in Libra, outer air over inner water. The mirror in the figure's image hints at reciprocity—beauty understood as negotiation. Like Albus, older lineages stemming from Islamic sources sometimes assign Puella entirely differently (often linking her with Venus in Taurus instead of Libra), but the Agrippan model firmly places her here. The figure is favorable but inclined to fickleness.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Courtship, the care of surfaces, diplomacy, the fair division of goods, regimens of grooming, the elegance of a settlement.

figures.name: Rubeus
figures.body_type: Skin that flushes readily, eyelids that hood under strong feeling, and a voice that drops in register when emotion rises.
figures.traditional_body_type: Classically associated with a rugged, powerfully built physique. Historical descriptions frequently mention a flushed or ruddy complexion prone to blemishes, alongside unruly hair and a deep voice.
figures.character_type: One who gives intimacy entirely or not at all, with a guarded streak of jealousy and an instinct to set the room in motion.
figures.traditional_character_type: Historically viewed as possessing a volatile, intense, and heavily passionate temperament. Older texts often warn of an inclination toward excess, fierce temperaments, and indulging in life's harsher extremes.
figures.colors: Red, flecked or streaked with brown
figures.commentary: Rubeus is the cup overturned: Mars in Scorpio, outer water over inner air. Passion that finds no upward outlet runs downward, and the medieval authors warned that this figure is good in evil things and evil in good ones. The practitioner must not moralize too quickly: at times Rubeus names a necessary surgery, a long-postponed honesty, or the investigation that will inevitably scorch its sources.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Intensity that strips the surface from a matter—the encounter that cannot remain decorous, the purge, the investigation, the long-postponed reckoning.
figures.tagline: Cup overturned, heat beneath the surface

figures.name: Acquisitio
figures.other_names: Grasping internally, inner wealth, something gained or picked up
figures.imagery: A bag held mouth upward, as though to take something in
figures.body_type: Broad hips and strong thighs, with a stride that covers ground efficiently. The hands accept what is offered without ceremony.
figures.traditional_body_type: Traditionally described as having a solidly packed, stocky build with a broad, expansive chest. Classical sources often note shorter limbs and a generally dense, forceful physical presence.
figures.character_type: An optimistic dealmaker who tends to believe that growth resolves most difficulties. Such a person speaks plainly, teaches what they know without pretense, and parts with their materials freely.
figures.traditional_character_type: Classically interpreted as robustly enthusiastic with an immense appetite for life. Historical texts emphasize a strong, unwavering commitment to fairness and justice, coupled with an expansive, confident personality.
figures.commentary: Acquisitio lifts the purse: Jupiter in Sagittarius, inner air over outer fire. The medieval authors paired the figure with prudence, since appetite must still sort the genuine from the false. The practitioner tracks the figure's enlargement in land held, lore gathered, health regained, and patronage reckoned plainly.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Increase obtained from a recognizable source—a raise, a grant, an inheritance, the upward motion of an investment, the news of a child, the growth of an audience, the late harvest.
figures.tagline: Receiving vessel, widening fortune, prudent appetite

figures.name: Carcer
figures.body_type: Pronounced knees, careful steps, and a tension that gathers in the jaw. Such a person tends toward sturdy footwear, organizes receipts with method, and visibly stiffens when the conversation turns to budgets or commitments.
figures.traditional_body_type: Historical descriptions point to a rigid, wiry frame characterized by visible physical tension, particularly in the shoulders and jaw. Classical texts note a tendency to cast the eyes downward.
figures.character_type: Frugal, stubborn, and loyal to whatever protocol they have accepted. The fear of disorder runs deeper than the fear of boredom.
figures.traditional_character_type: Traditionally viewed as highly conservative, cautious, and deeply inflexible. Older sources describe a character overly concerned with security, prone to hoarding resources, and resistant to change.
figures.commentary: Carcer is the lock and the ledger: Saturn in Capricorn, with earth doubled at the inner and outer registers. Energy meets matter without mediating elements, and work narrows to a single tunnel. The contemporary practitioner is left to ask whether the walls in question are protecting or suffocating—a contract, a savings instrument, a vow, a procedural hold.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Delay, the held deposit, the quarantine, the binding agreement, the fortified store, the long-term reserve, the institutional clock, the legal hold.

figures.name: Tristitia
figures.other_names: Crosswise, diminished, accursed, head down, fallen tower, cross
figures.imagery: A pit, a stake driven downward
figures.body_type: Heavy, well-set ankles and a preference for grounded footwear, with a deliberate, settling walk. Such a person is drawn to weighted objects.
figures.traditional_body_type: Classically depicted with a heavy, settling, or slightly stooped posture. Historical texts often describe a drawn, serious countenance and a complexion lacking vibrant color.
figures.character_type: Dry of wit, loyal once trust has been earned through long acquaintance, and inclined to think in systems. There is a strain of realism that can edge into the depressive register.
figures.traditional_character_type: Historically characterized by profound seriousness, a penchant for solitude, and a lingering melancholy. Older interpretations note an immense capacity for sustained, solitary labor but a tendency to hold long grudges.
figures.commentary: Tristitia drives the stake: Saturn in Aquarius, outer air over inner earth, with only earth active beneath three passive lines. The medieval authors named the figure sorrow, yet also recognized in it the foundation upon which towers may eventually stand if patience is allowed to do its work. Aquarius lifts the paradox into view: networks that freeze progress until the specifications improve.
figures.divinatory_meaning: A spell of low mood, a slide in valuation, the rumor of contraction, the work of digging, the long research, the funeral, the sober commitment.
figures.tagline: Weight downward, root deeper, truth slower

figures.name: Laetitia
figures.other_names: Bearded, laughing, singing, high tower, head lifted, candelabrum, high mountain
figures.body_type: A buoyant step and well-formed feet, a laugh that involves the whole torso, and hair worn somewhat freely. Such a person tends to go barefoot at home.
figures.traditional_body_type: Traditionally described as tall and broadly built, featuring large hands, feet, and facial proportions. Classical sources often paint a picture of a somewhat uncoordinated but imposing physique.
figures.character_type: Possessed of an innocent enthusiasm and a capacity for genuine awe. The temperament is given to the gambler's optimism and the swift forgiveness.
figures.traditional_character_type: Classically viewed as fundamentally good-natured, joyful, and deeply sincere. Historical texts often point to a profound, almost naive innocence and a strong inclination toward spiritual or religious devotion.
figures.commentary: Laetitia lifts the head: Jupiter in Pisces, inner fire over outer water, with fire alone active while its siblings rest—a torch raised against fog. The medieval joy figures warned that elevation invites visibility: the tower attracts the lightning. The practitioner therefore balances elation with discretion.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Promotion, public success, the spiritual lift, the rallying of sentiment, the news of a child, the season of celebration.
figures.tagline: Tower lights, uplifted spirit, bright hazard

figures.name: Cauda Draconis
figures.other_names: Outer threshold, threshold going out, lower boundary, stepping outside
figures.imagery: A doorway with footprints leading away from it
figures.body_type: A left arm that bears the marks of a long history, a posture that subtly turns away from a crowded room, and shoulders held a little unevenly.
figures.traditional_body_type: Historical texts frequently describe a form bearing the visible marks of hardship or age. Classical descriptions point to a worn appearance, perhaps featuring old scars, thinning hair, or a rugged asymmetry.
figures.character_type: A generosity that runs to depletion, an instinct to give until little remains and then to withdraw, and a guarded skepticism toward what may be received in return.
figures.traditional_character_type: Traditionally associated with a tendency toward dissolution and sudden severances. Older sources warn of a bitter or untrustworthy streak when cornered, alongside a fatalistic acceptance of loss.
figures.colors: Green, white, dark crimson, or pale tawny brown
figures.commentary: Cauda Draconis marks the threshold of the southern lunar node. While strictly lacking Planetary Intelligences or Spirits in the Agrippan model (hence 'None'), later Hermetic and Arabic practitioners often assigned Cauda the malefic properties of Saturn or Mars. The motion is not cruelty; it is completion with teeth. The figure releases what it carries, after the manner of a stage discarded once its work is done.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Closure, the residual risk that gathers at an exit, the formal end of a binding tie, graduation, the deliberate winding-down of an organization or regimen, resignation from work that has worn the querent down.
figures.tagline: Closure at the threshold; what exits carries consequence.

figures.name: Caput Draconis
figures.other_names: Inner threshold, threshold coming in, upper boundary, high tree, upright staff, stepping inside
figures.imagery: A doorway with footprints leading toward it
figures.body_type: A right arm conditioned to carry whatever new responsibility has been accepted—the working tool, the bag of provisions, the child.
figures.traditional_body_type: Classically depicted as well-proportioned, slender, and generally pleasing to the eye. Historical descriptions often highlight abundant hair and distinct, clear facial features.
figures.character_type: An earnest improver, given to method and to small acts of considered kindness. There is a recognizable anxiety before a major beginning.
figures.traditional_character_type: Historically characterized by an innate, steady kindness and a calm demeanor. Older texts emphasize a highly reliable, trustworthy nature that naturally seeks to nurture and build.
figures.commentary: Caput Draconis greets the threshold of the northern lunar node: earth doubled within and without, while air and water move and fire keeps watch—a fertile furrow. Like the Cauda, the Caput lacks formal Agrippan Intelligences, but Arabic and later occult traditions commonly assign it the benefic, expanding properties of Jupiter or Venus. Virgo refines appetite into craft. The practitioner should ask what seed is actually being planted.
figures.divinatory_meaning: The new offer of work, the news of a child, the formal invitation, the first stage of a project, the arrival of a mentor.
figures.tagline: A fertile threshold; beginnings ask disciplined tending.

figures.name: Fortuna Minor
figures.other_names: Outward fortune, protection going out, lesser omen, outside or apparent help
figures.imagery: A mountain with a staff atop it
figures.body_type: A straight spine and a quick pivot at the hip, with eyes that habitually read the horizon. The handshake is firm, but the attention is rarely settled in the room for long.
figures.traditional_body_type: Traditionally described as possessing a solid, slightly heavy build of average height. Classical sources note a rounded face, prominent features, and thick, often unmanageable hair.
figures.character_type: A proud helper, willing to shoulder the rescue when the moment calls for it. Such a person rises sharply on praise, accepts correction with humility after a misstep, and tends to share what they have generously.
figures.traditional_character_type: Classically viewed as outwardly boastful and fiercely proud, yet harboring hidden insecurities. Historical interpretations highlight a fundamentally generous, honor-bound nature beneath a blustering exterior.
figures.commentary: Fortuna Minor crowns the ridge: Sun in Leo, yet with outer air over inner fire. The classical contrast with the valley of Fortuna Major is exact: here, fortune rides on the wind. The gift comes from a referral, a sudden spotlight, a willing patron, or a moment of public attention. It is easily won and easily spent.
figures.divinatory_meaning: The brief win, the surge of attention, the borrowed ladder, the bonus that lands at the right moment, the moment of public favor.
figures.tagline: Swift favor from without; depth must be earned afterward.

figures.name: Via
figures.body_type: A stomach sensitive to anticipation, a body practiced at handling motion, and the small habits of one who travels often.
figures.traditional_body_type: Historical descriptions point to a body that carries weight lower down, often described as pear-shaped. Classical texts mention a tendency to perspire easily, a pale complexion, and softer, rounded features.
figures.character_type: A nomadic heart and a temperament that moves with its own tides. Such a person is loyal but needs new horizons to remain whole, prepares carefully for the road, and writes most clearly when between one place and the next.
figures.traditional_character_type: Traditionally characterized as highly mutable, restless, and deeply sensitive to environmental changes. Older sources emphasize a constant need for movement and a strong aversion to being tied down.
figures.commentary: Via opens every line: Moon in Cancer, water doubled inside and out, with all four elements active—a tidal highway. The medieval authors named the figure the road; today one may rightly add pilgrims' routes, post-roads, caravans, long migration, and the journey of identity. Nothing in this figure remains still; even sleep is the rhythm of cycles.
figures.divinatory_meaning: Relocation, change of lane, pivot, route, movement of households, goods, rumor, or kith—the long transition.
figures.tagline: Every line open; the stream keeps renewing its channel.
